state:early/view:academy:
Flight Academy

Learn to fly, one skill at a time

Short lessons you fly in MSFS while Trade Winds watches and coaches. With the sim connected, each step ticks itself off when you actually do it. Every lesson pays $150 toward your career.

0/14lessons complete
🎮

Lesson 1 · Ground school

Set up your controls

Most "the plane has a mind of its own" problems are controller setup: a stick that isn't centered, two devices fighting over one axis, or no dead zone.

10 min
🔑

Lesson 2 · Beginner

Engine start and taxi

Taxiing is where the flight starts.

10 min
🛫

Lesson 3 · Beginner

Your first takeoff

A good takeoff is smooth and boring: full power, straight down the centerline, lift off at the right speed, climb at the best rate..

10 min
⚖️

Lesson 4 · Beginner

Straight, level and trimmed

Trim takes the pressure off the controls so the plane flies itself.

10 min
🔄

Lesson 5 · Beginner

Turns without losing altitude

In a turn, part of the wing's lift tilts sideways, so the nose wants to drop.

10 min
⛽

Lesson 6 · Beginner

Mixture: what the co-pilot keeps telling you

Air gets thinner as you climb.

8 min
🪶

Lesson 7 · Intermediate

Flaps and speed limits

Flaps let you fly slower and descend steeper, but they have speed limits.

10 min
⚠️

Lesson 8 · Intermediate

Slow flight and stalls

A stall isn't the engine stopping.

12 min
⬜

Lesson 9 · Intermediate

Fly the traffic pattern

The pattern is a rectangle around the runway that every pilot flies the same way, so everyone knows where everyone else is.

15 min
🛬

Lesson 10 · Intermediate

The landing

Good landings come from good approaches.

15 min
🌬️

Lesson 11 · Advanced

Crosswind landing

The trade winds don't always blow straight down the runway.

15 min
🤖

Lesson 12 · Advanced

Autopilot basics

Autopilot is a tool for managing workload, not a replacement for flying.

8 min
🎧

Lesson 13 · Advanced

Talking to ATC in MSFS

MSFS's built-in ATC teaches the rhythm of real radio calls.

10 min
✈️

Lesson 14 · Real world

From sim to sky: becoming a pilot

Everything you just practiced is real.

5 min

state:early/hangar:msfs:
Live MSFS connection

Live sim off

The MSFS Bridge is a small program on your PC that reads MSFS 2020 or 2024 through SimConnect and hands this page your position, fuel and an automatic flight recording: block out, takeoff, touchdown rate, landing spot and block in. The debrief fills itself in from it.

  1. Install Node.js (LTS) if you don't have it.
  2. Unzip the msfs-bridge folder somewhere permanent, for example C:\Users\you\msfs-bridge, and double-click install.bat.
  3. In the Claude desktop app: Settings → Developer → Edit Config, and add the msfs-bridge entry from the README. Restart the Claude app.
  4. Open this page in the Claude desktop app on the same PC, start MSFS, and load into a flight.

It only works in the Claude desktop app on the PC running MSFS. In a browser or on your phone the career still works; you just log landings by hand.

state:midstory/hangar:msfs:
Live MSFS connection

Live sim off

The MSFS Bridge is a small program on your PC that reads MSFS 2020 or 2024 through SimConnect and hands this page your position, fuel and an automatic flight recording: block out, takeoff, touchdown rate, landing spot and block in. The debrief fills itself in from it.

  1. Install Node.js (LTS) if you don't have it.
  2. Unzip the msfs-bridge folder somewhere permanent, for example C:\Users\you\msfs-bridge, and double-click install.bat.
  3. In the Claude desktop app: Settings → Developer → Edit Config, and add the msfs-bridge entry from the README. Restart the Claude app.
  4. Open this page in the Claude desktop app on the same PC, start MSFS, and load into a flight.

It only works in the Claude desktop app on the PC running MSFS. In a browser or on your phone the career still works; you just log landings by hand.

Live MSFS connection

Live sim off

The MSFS Bridge is a small program on your PC that reads MSFS 2020 or 2024 through SimConnect and hands this page your position, fuel and an automatic flight recording: block out, takeoff, touchdown rate, landing spot and block in. The debrief fills itself in from it.

  1. Install Node.js (LTS) if you don't have it.
  2. Unzip the msfs-bridge folder somewhere permanent, for example C:\Users\you\msfs-bridge, and double-click install.bat.
  3. In the Claude desktop app: Settings → Developer → Edit Config, and add the msfs-bridge entry from the README. Restart the Claude app.
  4. Open this page in the Claude desktop app on the same PC, start MSFS, and load into a flight.

It only works in the Claude desktop app on the PC running MSFS. In a browser or on your phone the career still works; you just log landings by hand.

Learn to fly, one skill at a time

Short lessons you fly in MSFS while Trade Winds watches and coaches. With the sim connected, each step ticks itself off when you actually do it. Every lesson pays $150 toward your career.

0/14lessons complete
🎮

Lesson 1 · Ground school

Set up your controls

Most "the plane has a mind of its own" problems are controller setup: a stick that isn't centered, two devices fighting over one axis, or no dead zone.

10 min

Lesson 2 · Beginner

Engine start and taxi

Taxiing is where the flight starts.

10 min
🛫

Lesson 3 · Beginner

Your first takeoff

A good takeoff is smooth and boring: full power, straight down the centerline, lift off at the right speed, climb at the best rate..

10 min
⚖️

Lesson 4 · Beginner

Straight, level and trimmed

Trim takes the pressure off the controls so the plane flies itself.

10 min
🔄

Lesson 5 · Beginner

Turns without losing altitude

In a turn, part of the wing's lift tilts sideways, so the nose wants to drop.

10 min
⛽

Lesson 6 · Beginner

Mixture: what the co-pilot keeps telling you

Air gets thinner as you climb.

8 min
🪶

Lesson 7 · Intermediate

Flaps and speed limits

Flaps let you fly slower and descend steeper, but they have speed limits.

10 min
⚠️

Lesson 8 · Intermediate

Slow flight and stalls

A stall isn't the engine stopping.

12 min
⬜

Lesson 9 · Intermediate

Fly the traffic pattern

The pattern is a rectangle around the runway that every pilot flies the same way, so everyone knows where everyone else is.

15 min
🛬

Lesson 10 · Intermediate

The landing

Good landings come from good approaches.

15 min
🌬️

Lesson 11 · Advanced

Crosswind landing

The trade winds don't always blow straight down the runway.

15 min
🤖

Lesson 12 · Advanced

Autopilot basics

Autopilot is a tool for managing workload, not a replacement for flying.

8 min
🎧

Lesson 13 · Advanced

Talking to ATC in MSFS

MSFS's built-in ATC teaches the rhythm of real radio calls.

10 min
✈️

Lesson 14 · Real world

From sim to sky: becoming a pilot

Everything you just practiced is real.

5 min

Live MSFS connection

Live sim off

The MSFS Bridge is a small program on your PC that reads MSFS 2020 or 2024 through SimConnect and hands this page your position, fuel and an automatic flight recording: block out, takeoff, touchdown rate, landing spot and block in. The debrief fills itself in from it.

  1. Install Node.js (LTS) if you don't have it.
  2. Unzip the msfs-bridge folder somewhere permanent, for example C:\Users\you\msfs-bridge, and double-click install.bat.
  3. In the Claude desktop app: Settings → Developer → Edit Config, and add the msfs-bridge entry from the README. Restart the Claude app.
  4. Open this page in the Claude desktop app on the same PC, start MSFS, and load into a flight.

It only works in the Claude desktop app on the PC running MSFS. In a browser or on your phone the career still works; you just log landings by hand.

A fresh licence and a cheap job flying a Cessna in St. Martin. Then the mechanic asks you for a small favor. Five acts later you're flying a 747 full of contraband, and either running the Caribbean or running from it.

Create your pilot

Fly real jobs

Every job is a real flight you fly in MSFS 2020 or 2024: route, aircraft, weather and load, all planned for you.

Earn your wings

Checkrides from Commercial to Airline Transport Pilot, plus sign-offs for the world's scariest runways.

Build an airline

Buy used aircraft, finance them, set fares on your own routes, and watch your net worth grow (or not).

Mari wants you checked out in Coral Wing's Daher TBM 930 before the busy season. Your license doesn't cover it on your own yet, so she'll ride in the right seat as your instructor. Fly it to Arecibo, Puerto Rico and back to her standards, and she'll sign your logbook.

A turbine is smoother and more powerful than anything you've flown, and it eats fuel. Watch the torque and temperature limits on the takeoff roll.

What this flight teaches

  • Expect runway 08 at TJAB: about 17 kt of headwind and 3 kt of crosswind. The Daher TBM 930's demonstrated crosswind is around 25 kt.
  • Density altitude at TNCE is about 1,810 ft at 29 °C. The airplane performs as if the airport were that high, so expect a longer takeoff roll and a weaker climb.
  • International flight: Caribbean Netherlands to Puerto Rico (US). File a flight plan, carry your passport and the passengers' details, and clear customs and immigration on arrival.
  • Arriving in US airspace: altimeter settings are in inches of mercury and visibility in statute miles.
  • Night flight. Over water at night there's no horizon, so trust your attitude indicator and fly a stabilized approach to a lit runway.
  • First flight in the Daher TBM 930. One of the fastest single turboprops anywhere. Respect the torque on the takeoff roll. Speeds: Vr 90 · Vy 124 · Cruise 300 · Approach 85 KIAS.

Client briefing

Briefing

Mari wants you checked out in Coral Wing's Daher TBM 930 before the busy season. Your license doesn't cover it on your own yet, so she'll ride in the right seat as your instructor. Fly it to Arecibo, Puerto Rico and back to her standards, and she'll sign your logbook.

A turbine is smoother and more powerful than anything you've flown, and it eats fuel. Watch the torque and temperature limits on the takeoff roll.

Flight details: conditions, weights, route, aircraft and passengers

What this flight teaches

  • Expect runway 08 at TJAB: about 17 kt of headwind and 3 kt of crosswind. The Daher TBM 930's demonstrated crosswind is around 25 kt.
  • Density altitude at TNCE is about 1,810 ft at 29 °C. The airplane performs as if the airport were that high, so expect a longer takeoff roll and a weaker climb.
  • International flight: Caribbean Netherlands to Puerto Rico (US). File a flight plan, carry your passport and the passengers' details, and clear customs and immigration on arrival.
  • Arriving in US airspace: altimeter settings are in inches of mercury and visibility in statute miles.
  • Night flight. Over water at night there's no horizon, so trust your attitude indicator and fly a stabilized approach to a lit runway.
  • First flight in the Daher TBM 930. One of the fastest single turboprops anywhere. Respect the torque on the takeoff roll. Speeds: Vr 90 · Vy 124 · Cruise 300 · Approach 85 KIAS.

What this flight teaches

  • San Juan is busy airspace. Expect vectors, keep your speed up until they slow you, and brief the ILS early.
  • Expect runway 08 at TJSJ: about 10 kt of headwind and 2 kt of crosswind. The Cirrus Vision Jet G2's demonstrated crosswind is around 16 kt.
  • Density altitude at TUPJ is about 1,639 ft at 29 °C. The airplane performs as if the airport were that high, so expect a longer takeoff roll and a weaker climb.
  • International flight: British Virgin Islands to Puerto Rico (US). File a flight plan, carry your passport and the passengers' details, and clear customs and immigration on arrival.
  • Arriving in US airspace: altimeter settings are in inches of mercury and visibility in statute miles.
  • Read the METAR: wind 070° at 10 kt; visibility 10+ miles; few clouds at 2,500 ft, scattered clouds at 3,500 ft; 29 °C.

What this flight teaches

  • San Juan is busy airspace. Expect vectors, keep your speed up until they slow you, and brief the ILS early.
  • Expect runway 08 at TJSJ: about 14 kt of headwind and 2 kt of crosswind. The Cirrus Vision Jet G2's demonstrated crosswind is around 16 kt.
  • Density altitude at TUPJ is about 1,549 ft at 28 °C. The airplane performs as if the airport were that high, so expect a longer takeoff roll and a weaker climb.
  • International flight: British Virgin Islands to Puerto Rico (US). File a flight plan, carry your passport and the passengers' details, and clear customs and immigration on arrival.
  • Arriving in US airspace: altimeter settings are in inches of mercury and visibility in statute miles.
  • Read the METAR: wind 090° at 14 kt; visibility 10+ miles; few clouds at 2,500 ft, scattered clouds at 3,500 ft; 28 °C.

Briefing

A delivery yacht is leaving St Kitts for the Panama Canal at dawn, and half the crew is still on Sint Eustatius with their sea bags. Sea bags are soft, heavy and wet.

The skipper wants them aboard by sunset. Weigh the bags: sailors always underestimate.

Bonus objective (+$70): Land on the centerline: within 10 ft

What this flight teaches

  • Expect runway 07 at TKPK: about 2 kt of headwind and 0 kt of crosswind. The Grumman G-21 Goose's demonstrated crosswind is around 15 kt.
  • Density altitude at TNCE is about 1,420 ft at 25 °C. The airplane performs as if the airport were that high, so expect a longer takeoff roll and a weaker climb.
  • International flight: Caribbean Netherlands to St Kitts & Nevis. File a flight plan, carry your passport and the passengers' details, and clear customs and immigration on arrival.
  • First flight in the Grumman G-21 Goose. 1930s twin-engine flying boat. Antilles Air Boats flew Gooses around the Virgin Islands for decades. Speeds: Lift-off ~70 · Cruise 145 · Approach 80 KIAS.
  • Read the METAR: wind 080° at 2 kt; visibility 10+ miles; few clouds at 3,000 ft; 25 °C.

About this checkride

Briefing

Examiner Grace Wilkins meets you at the aircraft with a clipboard. Calm, fair and impossible to fool. Has given checkrides in every kind of weather the islands can produce.

"Fly it like I'm not here," she says. Jet Type Rating unlocks: Business jets: the Vision Jet and the Citation CJ4. Castillo is paying.

Flight details: conditions, weights, route, aircraft and passengers

What this flight teaches

  • Expect runway 06 at TNCE: about 12 kt of headwind and 7 kt of crosswind. The Cirrus Vision Jet G2's demonstrated crosswind is around 16 kt.
  • Density altitude at TNCE is about 1,690 ft at 28 °C. The airplane performs as if the airport were that high, so expect a longer takeoff roll and a weaker climb.
  • Read the METAR: wind 090° at 14 kt; visibility 10+ miles; few clouds at 2,500 ft, scattered clouds at 3,500 ft; 28 °C.
